messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: RStan vs. CmdStan timing (looks A-OK)
parts:
In working on a paper related to StataStan, Robert Grant
(author of StataStan) was finding odd timings, so I thought
I'd run a simple comparison. I used the following model:

parameters {
matrix[20,20] alpha[10];
}
model {
for (i in 1:10)
to_vector(alpha[i]) ~ normal(0, 1);
}

One chain of RStan and CmdStan run in almost exactly the
same time for the same seed. In this case, RStan's doing
even more work in that it's saving the warmup iterations,
whereas CmdStan isn't.

So it sure doesn't look like RStan is adding any overhead here.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan vs. CmdStan timing (looks A-OK)
parts: This was troubling me, so I re-ran it yesterday having shut down every other process (running under Windows, ho hum) I could. But I also think the Stata timings themselves look weird, as in they print a cumulative time (which makes sense) and an incremental time (which doesn't). This time I've taken the cumulative time and the strange pattern is gone. Lesson: use built-in timers by all means, but print the machine date/time to a log file at the same time as a sanity check.
